His substantial stake in Televisa's controlling company provided the financial base for ventures in telecommunications and sport after its sale. He also owned Atlante, the football club he moved from Mexico City to Cancún.

long_biography.plain_text:
Mextenis gave Alejandro Burillo Azcárraga a means of developing professional tennis in Mexico. He founded the organisation in 1992, shortly before Mexico City hosted its first ATP Tour event. His decision to move the Mexican Open from Mexico City to Acapulco in 2001 connected the tournament with a resort audience and room to expand its facilities.

He cultivated relationships with players, sponsors and tennis authorities as the event grew in international standing. The tournament changed from clay to hard courts. Mextenis also established the Abierto de Los Cabos, an ATP 250 tournament.
